title: Cryogenic 4D-STEM Study of Structural Evolution in Charged Polymers
content: Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) are soft materials, often polymers, that can efficiently transport and couple ionic and electronic charges, crucial for advancing bioelectronics and energy storage technologies [1]. To improve the efficiency and stability of OMIEC-based devices, it is crucial to understand their intrinsic structural properties and how they evolve under varying operational conditions. In this study, we combine cryo-EM with electrochemistry to fabricate TEM samples of polymeric OMIEC films in transient charged states under different operational conditions in aqueous electrolyte [2]. We characterize the polymer’s microstructure using 4D-STEM to explore the structural changes in the polymer across different states [3, 4]. Comparing the microstructures from the different charging levels reveals how charge density and electrochemical cycling can modify the polymer’s order and create structural heterogeneities. This approach enhances our understanding of the structural features that are pivotal to high OMIECs performance [6].
